submission.justification: Selection-S3 (neural-network classifier on kinematic variables) at 53% signal efficiency is the optimal choice, achieving an expected significance of 3.518 sigma. While Selection-S2 showed higher raw significance in initial studies (4.1 sigma at 50% efficiency), it must be rejected due to poor background modeling - the validation region study shows a 35% yield disagreement, which exceeds the agreed 10% tolerance. This is attributed to poorly modeled jet-substructure inputs. Selection-S3 demonstrates robust background estimation with only 6% yield disagreement (well within tolerance) while significantly outperforming the cut-based Selection-S1 (which peaks at 2.626 sigma at 60% efficiency). The 53% working point was determined by systematic scanning across the allowed 20-80% efficiency range, finding the maximum significance for Selection-S3.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible expected signal significance
